subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In the 1940s, the National Marine Research Center sought to understand why certain fish populations were declining in coastal waters.
• The center recruited marine biologist Rachel Carson to investigate the causes of these population changes.
• She analyzed water samples and tracked pollution sources from industrial facilities near the coastline.
• She succeeded in identifying chemical runoff as the primary factor harming fish reproduction.
prompt: The student wants to emphasize Rachel Carson's achievement. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: By analyzing water samples and tracking pollution sources from industrial facilities, Carson succeeded in identifying chemical runoff as the primary factor harming fish reproduction.
choices.B: In the 1940s, the National Marine Research Center, which recruited Carson, sought to understand declining fish populations in coastal waters.
choices.C: Carson was recruited by the National Marine Research Center at a time when fish population changes needed to be investigated.
choices.D: As part of efforts to understand fish population decline, water samples were analyzed and pollution sources from industrial facilities were tracked.

explanation: Choice A is the best answer. The sentence emphasizes Rachel Carson's achievement, explaining that she successfully identified chemical runoff as the primary factor harming fish reproduction by analyzing water samples and tracking pollution sources from industrial facilities.
